To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Boundary IoU is a more suitable evaluation metric than Mask IoU to evaluate boundary quality in object-centric segmentation tasks; (b) the Boundary IoU based Average Precision (Boundary AP) metric is a suitable evaluation metric for the instance segmentation task; (c) the Boundary IoIU based Panoptic Quality (Boundary PQ) metric is a better evaluation metric than the standard PQ for the panoptic segmentation task.

Boundary IoU, Boundary AP and Boundary PQ are more suitable for segmentation quality evaluation than existing metrics, and that the adoption of these new evaluation metrics will lead researchers to improve segmentation methods that better handle object boundaries.
